page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. However, memory bandwidth for read-only operations (both small and large blocks) is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and integer operations perform at average levels, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES.

The D4ads_v6 offers balanced resource allocation, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for general-purpose workloads that require local high-speed temporary storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized hardware. Due to the weak multi-threaded decompression and database operation benchmarks, it is less suited for heavy database engines or intensive compilation tasks. It is best fitted for web serving, text processing, Redis caching, and light-to-moderate analytical workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the Dadv6 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, placing in the top 25% of benchmarks. Multi-core execution and memory write bandwidth remain average, though read-only memory bandwidth is relatively weak. Lacking a GPU, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced workloads. It is highly suitable for static web serving, Redis caching, text processing, and general-purpose applications that benefit from fast local temporary storage but do not require massive memory configurations or heavy multi-threaded database operations.
